f1_peak_on_held_out.note: the F1-maximising cut if it were fitted on the held-out rows; computed to show the adopted cut landed near it, never adopted and never used to re-select anything

gap_against_cv.verdict: no measurable gap: the held-out PR-AUC sits 0.0155 above the CV mean, which is 0.92 bootstrap sd - and 15.4% of resampled draws of these same rows land below the CV mean, so a gap of this size is an ordinary draw rather than evidence either way
gap_against_cv.yardstick: the verdict divides the gap by the bootstrap sd of the held-out estimate, not by the CV sd: the CV sd is the spread between five models fitted to 28,934 rows each, while the bootstrap sd is the spread a single held-out estimate actually has
gap_against_cv.note: The CV figure describes a model fitted to 28,934 rows (four fifths of the training half) per fold; the artifact was fitted to all 36,168. The two numbers therefore answer slightly different questions, and the extra 7,234 rows predict a small gain rather than a loss.
